title: The scorecard's gate time counts the owner's judgings beside the tasks', for the fleet and for the mission whose gate judged them
prompt:
Read crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate/owner.rs (the owner's landings, `judge_owner` and the records it writes: `source.moved`, `source.push_refused`) and crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate/judging.rs (an owner judging's record and its gate time), crates/spawn-postgres/src/scorecard.rs (the FACTS statement: the record types it reads and the fields it keeps), crates/spawn-cli/src/scorecard/history.rs (`Record`, `GateRun`, `gated`) and crates/spawn-cli/src/scorecard/measure.rs (`gate_time` and its parts), and web/src/components/scorecard (where gate time is shown).

The problem, as the owner reads the Scorecard after 73e3596d (lead-mac, sync/queue.md 23:45; sync/page-scorecard-2026-11-11-2336.png). Since 11-10 owner pushes are judged by the integrator's gate: 42 judgings in 48 h, on the same gate slots as the fleet's tasks. None of them is counted anywhere.
- The fleet card says "Gate time 15m per gate run, n 242", from task gatings alone.
- Mission #7 (owner work on Spawn) says "not enough data (n 0)" and "gate time 0ms".
An owner judging's record carries its verdict and no gate time, and names no mission whose gate judged it. The scorecard reads gate runs from `task.gated` records only.

Required behaviour.
(a) The integrator's owner judging records carry `gate_ms` (the gate's wall clock, as `task.gated` carries it) and `mission` (the mission whose gate judged it). That applies to `source.moved` after a gated request, and to `source.push_refused` when the gate refused it.
(b) The scorecard's `gate_time` counts every gate run, a task's gating and an owner judging alike, in the fleet scope and in the scope of the mission named by the record. Its parts add `task_runs` and `owner_runs` beside `runs` (`runs` = `task_runs` + `owner_runs`).
(c) The Scorecard page's gate time says how many of its runs were the owner's.
(d) Records written before this change (no `gate_ms`) count as today: not at all.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/061.sh. Task records are written through `spawn_control_record`. Each owner landing is requested as `spawn mission push` records it, and its `source.moved` is recorded through `spawn_integrator_record` as the integrator records it. `spawn serve` answers. Gate missions 1 and 2 are on the same source:
- mission 1's tasks 1 and 2 are gated with `gate_ms` 600000 and 900000;
- mission 2's task 3 is gated with 400000;
- three owner landings carry `mission` 1 and `gate_ms` 1200000, 300000 and 450000. The store names `missions` [1, 2] on them: the missions a landing moves are not the mission whose gate judged it.
Read through `GET /api/scorecard?since=<1 h ago>`:
- (1) The fleet's `gate_time` is {value 450000, n 6, runs 6, task_runs 3, owner_runs 3}.
- (2) Mission 1's is {value 600000, n 5, runs 5, task_runs 2, owner_runs 3}. Mission 2's is {value null, n 1, runs 1, task_runs 1, owner_runs 0}: an owner judging counts for the mission named by `mission`, never for those in `missions`.
It fails with 1 on 73e3596d: the owner judgings are not counted, and there are no task_runs or owner_runs.

The product reason. The gate is the fleet's scarcest resource. Owner judgings take a growing share of it, and the scorecard leaves them out: it shows a cheaper, emptier gate than the one the fleet waits on, and an owner-work mission with no gate time at all. Counting them, and saying whose they were, shows the owner what the gate really costs and who uses it.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/, web/test/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green and add tests of your own for the new behaviour: a scorecard test through the real store (crates/spawn-postgres) that an owner judging's `gate_ms` is counted for the fleet and its mission, with task and owner counts unequal, and a record without `gate_ms` is not; an integrate test that the owner judging's records carry `gate_ms` and `mission`; and a web/test test for (c).
